title: Clinic Emergencies Drill — The First Five Minutes

hook.en: A patient goes grey and slides off the plinth. Another starts to wheeze after a new cream. A third shakes in the middle of the gym. In an emergency you are the first responder, and the first five minutes decide the outcome. Practise the response before you ever need it.
hook.ur: Ek mareez zard hokar plinth se phisal jata hai. Doosre ko nayi cream ke baad saans mein sansanahat hoti hai. Teesra gym ke beech mein kaanpne lagta hai. Emergency mein aap pehle responder hain, aur pehle paanch minute nateeja tay karte hain. Zaroorat se pehle jawab ki mashq karein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll follow one simple first response, recognise eight emergencies seen in clinics, take the first safe actions for each, know when to call emergency services, and prepare your clinic so the drill is automatic. This lesson does not replace a certified life-support course.
goal.ur: End tak aap ek saada pehla jawab apnayenge, clinics mein nazar aane wali aath emergencies pehchanenge, har ek ke pehle mehfooz qadam uthayenge, jaanenge ke emergency services kab bulani hain, aur apni clinic is tarah tayyar karenge ke drill khud ba khud ho jaye. Yeh lesson certified life-support course ki jagah nahi leta.

text.en: In every emergency the same **five-step first response** applies, whatever the cause: **Danger, Response, call for Help, Airway and Breathing, then Circulation (start compressions if needed)**. Make the area safe, check whether the patient answers, send someone to call for help and fetch the defibrillator, check the airway and breathing, and start chest compressions if the patient does not breathe normally. Everything else in this lesson is a variation on those five steps.
text.ur: Har emergency mein wohi **paanch qadam ka pehla jawab** lagu hota hai, wajah kuch bhi ho: **Danger, Response, Help bulayein, Airway aur Breathing, phir Circulation (zaroorat ho to compressions shuru)**. Jagah mehfooz banayein, dekhein ke mareez jawab deta hai ya nahi, kisi ko madad bulane aur defibrillator laane bhejein, airway aur saans dekhein, aur agar mareez normal saans nahi le raha to seene ki compressions shuru karein. Is lesson ki baaqi sab baatein in paanch qadmon ki shaklein hain.

text.en: Think of a **fire drill**. Nobody reads the manual while the building burns: everyone already knows the exit, the meeting point and who calls the fire brigade. An emergency drill works the same way. The more clearly the roles and the equipment are fixed in advance, the less you have to think when your heart is racing.
text.ur: **Fire drill** sochein. Imaarat jalte waqt koi manual nahi parhta: har koi pehle se exit, jama hone ki jagah aur fire brigade bulane wale ko jaanta hai. Emergency drill bhi yunhi chalta hai. Roles aur saman jitna pehle se tay hon, utna kam sochna padta hai jab dil tez dhadak raha ho.

steps.title: Danger
steps.detail: Make sure the area is safe for you and the patient. Move equipment, switch off power, call for help early. || Danger

steps.title: Response
steps.detail: Tap the shoulders and ask loudly, "Can you hear me?" If there is no answer, treat the patient as unresponsive. || Response

steps.title: Help
steps.detail: Shout for help and send a named person to call emergency services and bring the defibrillator and the emergency kit. Say the address and the problem clearly. || Help

steps.title: Airway and Breathing
steps.detail: Open the airway by tilting the head and lifting the chin. Look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than ten seconds. Gasping is not normal breathing. || Airway aur Breathing

steps.title: Circulation
steps.detail: If the patient is not breathing normally, start chest compressions in the centre of the chest, at a rate of 100 to 120 a minute, pushing at least 5 centimetres but not more than 6 in an adult, and attach the defibrillator as soon as it arrives. || Circulation

title.en: Eight clinic emergencies: what you see, what you do first, and when to call
title.ur: Clinic ki aath emergencies: kya nazar aata hai, pehle kya karna hai, aur kab bulana hai

rows.en: Collapse, no normal breathing
rows.ur: Gir parna, normal saans nahi

rows.en: Five-step response, compressions, defibrillator as soon as it arrives
rows.ur: Paanch qadam jawab, compressions, defibrillator aate hi

rows.en: Always, at once
rows.ur: Hamesha, foran

rows.en: Faint (syncope)
rows.ur: Behoshi (syncope)

rows.en: Lay flat, raise the legs, check breathing and response, loosen tight clothing
rows.ur: Seedha litayein, taangein oonchi, saans aur jawab dekhein, tang kapray dheelay

rows.en: If not waking within a minute, not breathing normally, injured, chest pain or palpitations first
rows.ur: Aik minute mein hosh na aaye, saans normal na ho, chot ho, ya pehle seene ka dard ya dhadkan thi

rows.en: Chest pain or suspected heart attack
rows.ur: Seene ka dard ya mumkin heart attack

rows.en: Stop activity, sit him comfortably, take pulse and pressure, keep him calm, no walking
rows.ur: Activity rokein, aaram se bithayein, nabz aur pressure naapein, sukoon se rakhein, chalne na dein

rows.en: At once if pain lasts beyond a few minutes, with sweating, breathlessness or nausea
rows.ur: Foran agar dard chand minute se zyada, paseena, saans ki tangi ya matli ke saath

rows.en: Stroke
rows.ur: Stroke

rows.en: Check face, arm, speech: drooping, weak arm, slurred speech; note the time it started; keep him still
rows.ur: Chehra, bazu, zubaan dekhein: dhalka chehra, kamzor bazu, lukknat; shuru hone ka waqt likhein; sakin rakhein

rows.en: At once: time is brain
rows.ur: Foran: waqt dimagh hai

rows.en: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)
rows.ur: Shadeed allergy (anaphylaxis)

rows.en: Remove the trigger, lay flat with legs raised (sit up if breathing is hard), use the patient's own adrenaline pen if you are trained, stay with him
rows.ur: Wajah hatayein, taangein oonchi karke seedha litayein (saans mushkil ho to bithayein), agar training hai to mareez ka apna adrenaline pen istemal karein, saath rahein

rows.en: At once
rows.ur: Foran

rows.en: Low blood sugar
rows.ur: Kam blood sugar

rows.en: If awake and able to swallow: fast sugar such as glucose tablets or sweet juice by your protocol, recheck in 15 minutes; never put food in the mouth of someone who is not alert
rows.ur: Hoshiyar aur nigal sakta ho to: protocol ke mutabiq glucose goliyan ya meetha juice, 15 minute baad dobara dekhein; jo hoshiyar na ho uske muh mein kuch na daalein

rows.en: Not fully awake, fitting, or not recovering
rows.ur: Poori tarah hoshiyar nahi, daura, ya theek nahi ho raha

rows.en: Seizure
rows.ur: Daura

rows.en: Note the time, protect the head, clear space, do not hold him down or put anything in the mouth, roll to the side when it stops
rows.ur: Waqt likhein, sar ki hifazat, jagah saaf, pakren nahi aur muh mein kuch nahi daalein, ruknay par karwat dilayein

rows.en: Over five minutes, repeating, injured, first seizure, not recovering, or trouble breathing
rows.ur: Paanch minute se zyada, dohrata hua, chot, pehla daura, thek nahi ho raha, ya saans mein mushkil

rows.en: Choking
rows.ur: Dam ghutna

rows.en: Encourage coughing if he can cough or speak; if he cannot breathe, cough or speak, use the back blows and abdominal thrusts taught in your certified course
rows.ur: Khansi ki hausla afzai agar khans ya bol sakta ho; agar saans, khansi ya bolna nahi ho sakta to apne certified course mein sikhaye back blows aur abdominal thrusts

rows.en: If severe, or if he becomes unresponsive: start compressions
rows.ur: Shadeed ho, ya behosh ho jaye: compressions shuru

question.en: A patient collapses on the plinth. He does not answer when you shout and tap his shoulders, and he is only gasping occasionally. What do you do?
question.ur: Mareez plinth par gir jata hai. Aap ke pukarne aur kandhay thapthapane par jawab nahi deta, aur kabhi kabhi sirf hanphta hai. Aap kya karein?

text.en: Sit him up and give him water

feedback.en: An unresponsive patient could choke, and sitting up delays the response.
feedback.ur: Behosh mareez ka dam ghut sakta hai, aur bithane se jawab mein der hoti hai.

text.en: Wait a minute to see if he starts breathing normally
text.ur: Ek minute intezar karein ke woh normal saans lene lagta hai ya nahi

feedback.en: Waiting wastes the minutes that matter most.
feedback.ur: Intezar un minuton ko zaya karta hai jo sab se ahem hain.

text.en: Treat as cardiac arrest: call for help and a defibrillator, and start chest compressions at once
text.ur: Cardiac arrest samjhein: madad aur defibrillator bulayein, aur foran seene ki compressions shuru karein

feedback.en: Yes — gasping is not normal breathing, and early compressions and a defibrillator save lives.
feedback.ur: Haan — hanphna normal saans nahi, aur jaldi compressions aur defibrillator jaan bachate hain.

question.en: A patient starts convulsing on the floor. What is the correct first response?
question.ur: Mareez zameen par jhatkay lene lagta hai. Sahi pehla jawab kya hai?

text.en: Note the time, protect his head and clear the space, and roll him onto his side when the movements stop
text.ur: Waqt likhein, sar ki hifazat aur jagah saaf karein, aur jhatkay ruknay par karwat dilayein

feedback.en: Yes — protect and time the seizure; do not restrain it.
feedback.ur: Haan — daure ki hifazat aur waqt likhein; ise rokein nahi.

text.en: Hold his arms and legs firmly to stop the movements
text.ur: Jhatkay rokne ke liye hath paon mazbooti se pakren

feedback.en: Restraining can cause injury and does not stop a seizure.
feedback.ur: Pakarne se chot lag sakti hai aur daura nahi rukta.

text.en: Put a spoon or a wallet in his mouth to protect his tongue
text.ur: Zubaan ki hifazat ke liye muh mein chamach ya purse daalein

feedback.en: That can break teeth or block the airway.
feedback.ur: Isse daant toot sakte hain ya airway band ho sakti hai.

question.en: A diabetic patient on insulin is sweating, shaky and confused but can still drink. What is the best first action?
question.ur: Insulin lene wala diabetes ka mareez paseenay mein, kaanpta aur uljha hua hai lekin pee sakta hai. Behtareen pehla qadam kya hai?

text.en: Give fast sugar by your clinic protocol, such as glucose tablets or sweet juice, stay with him and recheck in about 15 minutes
text.ur: Clinic protocol ke mutabiq tez sugar dein, jaise glucose goliyan ya meetha juice, saath rahein aur takreeban 15 minute baad dobara dekhein

feedback.en: Yes — quick sugar treats low blood sugar, and he must be watched until fully recovered.
feedback.ur: Haan — tez sugar kam blood sugar ka ilaaj hai, aur mukammal theek hone tak nigrani zaroori hai.

text.en: Make him do light exercise to burn it off
text.ur: Halki exercise karwayen taake kam ho jaye

feedback.en: Exercise lowers the sugar still more.
feedback.ur: Exercise sugar ko mazeed kam karti hai.

text.en: Give him a tablet of insulin to even things out
text.ur: Barabar karne ke liye insulin dein

feedback.en: Insulin would drop the sugar further.

text.en: **Waiting until you are sure.** Many people delay the call because they think, "He might just be tired." In real emergencies the cost of calling too early is a few minutes of a paramedic's time; the cost of calling too late can be a life. Call first, assess while help is coming. Equally, do not stand a fainted patient up quickly, and do not stop compressions to check if "it is working".
text.ur: **Yaqeen hone ka intezar karna.** Bohat se log call mein der karte hain kyunke sochte hain, "Shayad bas thak gaya hai." Asal emergencies mein bohat jaldi call karne ki qeemat paramedic ke chand minute hai; bohat der se call karne ki qeemat jaan ho sakti hai. Pehle call karein, madad aate hue assess karein. Aur behosh hue mareez ko jaldi se khara na karein, aur compressions ko yeh dekhne ke liye na rokein ke "kaam kar rahi hain".

text.en: **Prepare before you need it.** Make a one-page emergency plan: the address to say on the phone, the emergency number, who calls, who fetches the equipment, where the defibrillator, oxygen, glucose and the emergency kit are, and who writes the times. Run a five-minute drill every month. Afterwards, tell the family what happened and what you did, record the times and actions in the notes, and report the event as your service requires.
text.ur: **Zaroorat se pehle tayyari karein.** Ek safha ka emergency plan banayein: phone par bolne ka pata, emergency number, kaun call karega, kaun saman layega, defibrillator, oxygen, glucose aur emergency kit kahan hain, aur waqt kaun likhega. Har mahine paanch minute ka drill karein. Baad mein khandan ko batayein kya hua aur aap ne kya kiya, notes mein waqt aur qadam likhein, aur wakiye ko apni service ke taqaze ke mutabiq report karein.

question.en: Why should you start compressions even if you are not sure the patient is in cardiac arrest?
question.ur: Aap ko compressions tab bhi kyun shuru karni chahiye jab yaqeen na ho ke mareez cardiac arrest mein hai?

answer.en: Because the harm from compressions in someone who does not need them is small, while the harm of withholding them in someone who does is huge. Guidelines therefore tell untrained and trained people alike to begin compressions for anyone who is unresponsive and not breathing normally.
answer.ur: Kyunke jis ko zaroorat nahi us par compressions ka nuqsan chhota hai, jabke jis ko zaroorat hai us se rokne ka nuqsan bohat bara hai. Isliye guidelines tarbiyat yaafta aur be-tarbiyat dono ko kehti hain ke jo behosh ho aur normal saans na le uske liye compressions shuru karein.

beats.patient: A 62-year-old woman is doing leg exercises when she suddenly goes pale, says she feels dizzy, and slumps in the chair. She answers when you speak to her and is breathing. Her pulse is slow and weak.
beats.assessment: She has fainted or nearly fainted; she is responding and breathing, which excludes cardiac arrest for now. Slow, weak pulse is concerning, so a cause such as the heart rhythm, low pressure or low sugar must be considered.
beats.treatment: Lay her flat or recline her with her legs raised, check breathing and response again, loosen tight clothing, check pulse, pressure and sugar if available, and call for help if she is not quickly improving. Do not sit her up fast.
beats.reassess: She recovers within a minute, but with a slow pulse you arrange a medical review the same day instead of sending her home, and you record the times and findings.

text.en: **Know your limits and your training.** This lesson does not replace a certified life-support course; do one every year. Use only the equipment and actions you are trained and permitted to use, follow your clinic protocol, and call emergency services early. Never delay the call to look for a cause, and never leave a patient alone after an emergency until help has taken over.
text.ur: **Apni hudood aur training jaanein.** Yeh lesson certified life-support course ki jagah nahi leta; har saal ek course karein. Sirf wohi saman aur qadam istemal karein jin ki training aur ijazat ho, clinic protocol par chalein, aur emergency services jaldi bulayein. Wajah dhoondne ke liye call mein der kabhi na karein, aur emergency ke baad jab tak madad na sambhal le mareez ko akela na chhorein.

text.en: The American Heart Association resuscitation guidelines advise starting chest compressions for an adult who is unresponsive and not breathing normally, at 100 to 120 per minute, 5 to 6 centimetres deep, allowing full recoil, and using a defibrillator as early as possible; early compressions and early defibrillation are the strongest links in survival. Resuscitation Council guidance for anaphylaxis stresses early intramuscular adrenaline and calling emergency services without delay.
text.ur: American Heart Association ke resuscitation guidelines kehte hain ke baaligh jo behosh ho aur normal saans na le uske liye seene ki compressions shuru karein, 100 se 120 prati minute, 5 se 6 centimeter gehri, poori wapsi ki ijazat ke saath, aur defibrillator jaldi se jaldi istemal karein; jaldi compressions aur jaldi defibrillation zinda bachne ke sab se mazboot kari hain. Anaphylaxis ke liye Resuscitation Council ki rehnumai jaldi intramuscular adrenaline aur bina der emergency services bulane par zor deti hai.

text.en: **DR-H-ABC.** Danger, Response, Help, Airway and Breathing, Circulation. Say it out loud until it is automatic.
text.ur: **DR-H-ABC.** Danger, Response, Help, Airway aur Breathing, Circulation. Isay zor se kahein jab tak khud ba khud na ho jaye.

summary.en: Use the same five steps in every emergency: Danger, Response, Help, Airway and Breathing, Circulation.
summary.ur: Har emergency mein wohi paanch qadam: Danger, Response, Help, Airway aur Breathing, Circulation.

summary.en: Unresponsive and not breathing normally means start compressions and call for a defibrillator at once; call early for any serious emergency.
summary.ur: Behosh aur normal saans nahi to foran compressions aur defibrillator bulayein; har serious emergency mein jaldi call karein.

summary.en: Prepare a clinic plan, practise it every month and train in a certified life-support course every year.
summary.ur: Clinic ka plan banayein, har mahine mashq karein aur har saal certified life-support course karein.

front.en: How fast are adult chest compressions?
front.ur: Baalighon ki compressions kitni tez hoti hain?

back.en: 100 to 120 a minute, 5 to 6 centimetres deep.
back.ur: 100 se 120 prati minute, 5 se 6 centimeter gehri.

back.en: No: treat it as not breathing normally.
back.ur: Nahi: ise normal saans nahi samjhein.

front.en: What do you never do during a seizure?
front.ur: Daure ke dauran kya kabhi nahi karte?

back.en: Hold the patient down or put anything in the mouth.
back.ur: Mareez ko pakarna ya muh mein kuch daalna.

front.en: Who should you call first in a serious emergency?
front.ur: Serious emergency mein pehle kise bulayein?

back.en: Emergency services, then assess while help comes.
back.ur: Emergency services, phir madad aate hue assess karein.
